title: Gamo Amicho
community: Gamo people — Arba Minch region, Rift Valley lakes
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Gamo Amicho — boiled yam or false yam (Dioscorea) dressed with butter, berbere, and salt. The staple food of the Gamo people around Arba Minch and the Rift Valley lakes — the root vegetable tradition that complements the fish of the lake region.
longDesc: Amicho is the Gamo alternative to injera — boiled and dressed with the simplest of preparations, the false yam or true yam provides the starchy base that accompanies fish from the nearby Rift Valley lakes.
ingredients: 800g yam (or sweet potato as substitute) — peeled, cubed
steps: Boil yam in salted water 20—25 minutes until very tender.
Dress with butter or kibbeh, berbere, and salt while hot.
chefTips: Dress while hot — the butter melts and absorbs into the yam.
commonMistakes: Dressing cold yam — butter doesn't absorb.
cookingScience: Yam starch gelatinises during boiling. The warm yam's surface channels and pores absorb the melted butter through capillary action — producing a uniform seasoning throughout.
sustainabilityTips: Gamo yams — grown in the Rift Valley without irrigation.
healthBenefits: Yam is high in vitamin B6 and potassium.
culturalNote: Gamo Amicho is the lakeside staple — eaten with the fresh fish from the Rift Valley lakes that has sustained the Gamo people for centuries.
